subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP/sub-agent thread messages bypass busy channel or reply-operation admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a successor be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent routing contract affects message ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Refresh the admission PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path or replace it with a rebased branch that preserves terminal recovery and makes accepted queue-policy turns explicit.

options.title: Limit steering to explicit controls
options.body: Keep ordinary messages queued for now and document command-only steering until maintainers choose a safer active-session ingress design.

options.title: Split channel-specific tracking
options.body: Keep the broad queue-steering issue canonical and retain this issue only for Discord ACP/thread-specific validation if maintainers want separate acceptance proof.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path or replace it with a rebased branch that preserves terminal recovery and makes accepted queue-policy turns explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on active/non-streaming steering and adjacent reply-run lifecycle behavior that the remaining route must preserve.
